Use the Omni-GM split-scenes procedure to begin recording a new invented session dated 2026-01-03 in a new adventure "The Glass Causeway no-shell proof". You have no shell or file tools. I have the original transcript file on my computer. Here is its text for context:
[00:00:00] GM: You reach the Glass Causeway at dusk. The river gate closes in four bells.
[00:01:10] GM as Sera Venn: Mind the stones, dear. My ferry is waiting. She speaks softly, then snaps the last word.
[00:02:20] Rowan: Sarah Ven seems nervous. I bet she works for the raiders.
[00:03:00] GM as Sera Venn: Some say the Lantern Widow lives beneath the bridge. I have never seen her.
[00:04:00] GM: Sera Venn shows you a broken seal. The gate clock has four segments, one filled; you can all see it.
[00:05:10] Rowan: I want to ask the gatekeeper about that seal tomorrow.
[00:07:00] GM: At the ferry landing, the gatekeeper leaves a red cord tied to the post. You are still here at dusk.
Map GM as the game master and Rowan and Mira as players. Follow the procedure. Do not invent that a file upload has occurred. Stop when the next step requires me.
note: Invented fixture. Upload capabilities, provider usage and thinking omitted. Hooks disabled for this run.

{"name":"split-scenes","procedure":"If the session has no stored transcript, call transcript_upload_url. With a shell and a file on disk, run curl -T <file> <signed-url> directly from disk. Never read, echo, cat or repeat the file to upload it. The signed URL is single-use and expires after ten minutes.
Without a shell or without the original file on disk, immediately give the game master pageUrl to sign in and upload the original transcript file. Pause until they have uploaded it. Do not retype the transcript in tool calls or chat, even when you hold it in context.
Both paths use UTF-8 [HH:MM:SS] Speaker: text with continuation lines, at most 8 MB and 20000 utterances, 32 KB per utterance including continuations. Upload before scenes or draft changes exist. Read get transcript:<session> to confirm it is stored before mapping speakers, splitting scenes or starting the debrief. If the transcript is still missing, wait for the upload.
Load skill map-speakers and map the speakers. Read get transcript:<session> in pages or timestamp windows; follow nextCursor as cursor with the same ref while truncated. Never repeat the transcript in output.
Split into scenes at changes of place or situation. Give each a short title, start and optional end timestamp, place and a summary of plot points in one or two lines. Keep the original timestamps. Do not overlap scenes. Leave out rolls, rests, hit points and inventory.
Call scenes_set with the session and scenes in order. Use get scene:<session>/<n> to check a scene with its utterances. Splitting replaces earlier scenes, so drop existing draft changes first; a committed debrief and its scenes are closed.

Standing rules
Never draft prep. Propose only on the game master's explicit request, at most three situations built from story-state facts with sources.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}
